claims.statement: New EU repair rights have applied since 31 July 2026, extend seller liability by at least 12 months when repair is chosen, and require accessible repair information and reasonable access to repair.
Consumers currently pay repairers for covered appliance and electronics repairs, while manufacturers and sellers bear intake, routing, parts, and guarantee-administration costs.
A manufacturer, retailer, insurer, or repair network may pay per routed case; the future EU platform may reduce their willingness to use a private router.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: After-sales service, warranty, or operations director
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: The planned public EU platform will aid discovery; private value must come from triage, capacity confirmation, SLA routing, and case evidence
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed contracts with repair networks and retailers
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: White-label retailer intake, insurer partnerships, and search acquisition

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 20,000-80,000 PLN per anchor retailer or 50-150 PLN per consumer repair
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Platform minimum monthly plus per completed repair
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 45-65% after intake support and payment costs
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: automated triage with 5-15 minutes human exception time per case
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Consumer law, payment terms, warranty boundaries, insurance, and GDPR
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Per completed repair plus network software fee
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Consumer acquisition, triage, payment processing, disputes, and repairer onboarding

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Retailers, manufacturers, and the EU platform improve native repair routing
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current consumer repair payments and business labor spent diagnosing, quoting, locating capacity, routing parts, and documenting warranty extensions
commercial_mechanics.payer: Retailer, manufacturer, insurer, repair network, or consumer depending channel
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Repair request for a covered product, unavailable local capacity, or retailer warranty intake
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Each repair transaction; annual network contracts

contrary_evidence: A European repair platform is expected in 2027 and may commoditize discovery.
Repair quality and economics vary sharply by product and geography.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed nonexclusive repairer capacity reservations and retailer intake agreements; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Operate as a quote-comparison directory without guaranteed slots or warranty routing
critical_control_point.current_owner: Repairers control capacity; retailers and manufacturers control warranty intake
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed contracts with repair networks and retailers
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No current repair capacity, retailer intake, or customer relationship is controlled
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business after counterparties reserve slots; repairers control fulfillment
critical_control_point.subject: Verified local repair capacity and triaged case routing

economics.acquisition_route: Start in Warsaw with one appliance category, manually validate ten repairers, route 100 paid cases, then sell white-label intake
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 50,000 annual completed repairs at 100 PLN net revenue yields 5m PLN revenue; at 15% owner earnings plus network equity, 5m PLN net worth may take 7-12 years. Capacity density, CAC, and disputes are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours weekly initially; dispatch and support need hiring before scale
economics.gross_margin_basis: Transaction and platform revenue less acquisition, triage, payment, and dispute costs
economics.payback: Assumption: consumer CAC payback within the first job; enterprise acquisition within 18 months
economics.pricing: Assumption: 50-150 PLN platform revenue per completed repair plus 2,000-10,000 PLN monthly white-label minimum
economics.retention_or_repeat: Low consumer frequency but repeated retailer volume and repairer utilization

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Failure-mode, quote, completion, and repairer reliability data
fingerprint.customer: Retailers and consumers needing covered appliance repair
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label retail intake and local search
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Retailer or consumer pays when a repair is booked and completed
fingerprint.problem_trigger: New repair rights increase formal repair intake and warranty administration

founder_fit: Founder can build data-driven triage and reliability scoring.
Warsaw offers a dense pilot geography.
Operations are measurable, though more people-intensive than preferred.
risks: The public platform may disintermediate discovery.
Repair disputes and low-quality providers can damage trust.
Marketplace operations may exceed part-time capacity.

structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: reserved verified repair slots by category and postcode

structure.control_point: Verified repair slots linked to diagnostic intake
structure.critical_dependency: Repairer density, quality, and public-platform positioning

thesis: The newly applicable right-to-repair regime shifts repair from informal discovery toward documented intake, creating room for a capacity-aware router before the public platform matures.
title: Repair Intake and Capacity Router
uncertainties: Case volume caused by the new rules is unknown.
Repairer willingness to reserve capacity is unknown.
Who will pay the routing fee is unresolved.
